analysis.title: US Market Intelligence | Morning Briefing (October 14, 2026)
key_insights: JPM Market Intel is Tactically Bullish on US equities into earnings season and updated its Monetization Menu, with a preference for Tech and some Cyclicals and the AI theme as a globally bullish view.

Semis/Memory trade did not restart after ASML's beat-and-raise: SOX had five straight down sessions (longest losing streak since July) and MU is -1.2% to -1.4% pre-market. TSMC earnings Thursday and a frontier model investor event today are the near-term drivers.

ASML Q3 was a margin-led beat with FY26 sales guide raised. Revisions going in were low-single-digit versus ~30% last print, and the stock is up versus down last time. Scott Silver says the earlier disappointment was about the lack of clarity on 2027 and capacity, not the numbers.

Sept CPI is due at 8:30am ET. Feroli sees headline MoM +0.55% (3.6% YoY) and core MoM +0.18% (2.4% YoY). JPM says that print should keep the bond market from pricing an October hike, with a skip and a December hike still seen as most likely.
If core MoM comes in near 0.18%, JPM expects yields to fall globally, supporting rate-sensitive baskets, and flags a possible squeeze post-CPI with tech front and center.

Day 1 bank earnings read-through is bullish on the US consumer and credit. Card spend grew 10% YoY at JPM and 13% at C, and delinquencies and net credit losses are falling YoY at C and WFC. Corporate credit is healthy at C, and the labor market is cited as the support.

Chase spending data shows total September spending +6.6% YoY, up from +5.3% in August. Upper, middle and lower income cohorts were +7.8%, +8.2% and +6.6%. August wage growth was 4.7% for lower, 3.8% for middle and 3.7% for higher income households.

JPM Retail basket (JP2RTL) is down 8.7% from its August peak on affordability and rising yields. Retail L/S ratio is at the 37th percentile and Consumer Discretionary at the 38th (data as of Oct 8, 2025), so positioning is light.

JPM financials specialist Rob O'Dwyer calls the bank-stock weakness 'head scratching', likely quant/passive flow. He argues the flatter curve is not a good reason to sell banks since the front end is basically unchanged, and says the move is a reason to fade and buy the group. Re-grossing into the print is a small technical headwind.

WFC guided 4Q NIM stable QoQ with NII pace increasing, expects 4Q26 loan growth above mid-single-digit YoY, and sees no broad-based credit deterioration. Citi's ROTCE comments disappointed investors, but O'Dwyer thinks Citi is sandbagging and sees FY ROTCE nearer 12%.

Semis view: SOX is ~20% off its July lows and ~15% below its June highs. JPM thinks Semis can climb the wall of worry on Hynix/Samsung updates, and expects breadth, which keeps deteriorating, to reverse around earnings.
Market pricing: a Dec hike and then 2 hikes in FY27. Lower bond yields from dovish inflation prints are named as a catalyst. Fed day is Oct 28.
Reopening theme (Cruise Lines, Hotels, Retailers) is on the shopping list given consumer strength and insulation from high energy prices. Internationally, ex-AI, JPM likes Brazil and Japan.

Earlier menus: keep Tech as a core long but drop the RTY short pairing on squeeze risk from lower oil or yields, and use derivatives to play the squeeze. Favor Banks ex-AI. A US/Iran deal is the biggest catalyst and would squeeze EU and RTY higher.
Overnight geopolitical headlines are escalatory (Houthis hitting Aramco HQ, Iran's new Strait of Hormuz tactics). WTI is +0.7% at $94.74. Silver fell to its lowest since August.

market_movers.rationale: Margin-led Q3 beat and raised FY26 sales guide lifted the stock about 1.3%. Scott Silver notes the market rewarded good numbers, unlike July.
Memory continued to underperform, with MU down 1.2% to 1.4% pre-market despite the ASML beat.
Guided 4Q NIM stable and NII rising, with healthy C&I loan demand and no broad credit deterioration.
ROTCE comments disappointed investors, but JPM's O'Dwyer thinks Citi is sandbagging and sees FY ROTCE nearer 12%.

sector_views.rationale: Tactically bullish. Semis and Mag7 may outperform the Tech tape and earnings should add support.
Strong spending data, bank card data and cash levels support the consumer. Q3 earnings are a catalyst and positioning is light.
Growth reboot, a potentially steeper curve and a favorable capital markets outlook. O'Dwyer says to fade the recent weakness.
Reopening theme names are insulated from elevated energy prices and supported by consumer strength.
Rate-sensitive sectors may join a squeeze but are most likely to lag the SPX ex-AI.

earnings_insights: ASML Q3 (reported 10/14 morning): margin-led beat, FY26 sales guide raised. Revisions going in were low-single-digit versus about 30% before the last print.
JPM (reported 10/13): debit and credit spend +10% YoY, and card net charge-off rate still expected at about 3.2%.

Citi (reported 10/13): spend volume +13%, average loans +9%, partly offset by private label card declines. Cards net credit loss and delinquency rates fell YoY, and corporate non-accruals and net credit losses stayed low. ROTCE comments were seen as unsatisfactory, with JPM's O'Dwyer expecting FY ROTCE near 12%.
WFC (reported 10/13): charge-off ratio down from Q2 and a year ago, early-stage delinquencies at historic lows. 4Q NIM expected stable QoQ, and 4Q26 loan growth expected above mid-single-digit YoY.
Earnings due 10/14: BAC, BLK, FAST, MS, PGR, STT. TSMC reports Thursday 10/15. Q3 consumer earnings are cited as a positive catalyst.

macro_indicators.interpretation: A headline increase driven by energy, with the print due 8:30am ET on 10/14.
A soft core print would keep the market from pricing an October hike and push yields lower globally.

macro_indicators.reading: Dec hike, then 2 hikes in FY27

Brazil/Latam is attractive irrespective of AI views, since AI fear may push the market into non-AI plays.

Spike in bond vol or equity vol.
Higher prices weighing on lower-income household sentiment.
Escalation in the Middle East pushing oil higher.
Breadth deterioration and fragile AI sentiment.
vol_and_positioning: Retail (JP2RTL) L/S ratio is at the 37th percentile since Jan 2018 and Consumer Discretionary (JP2CND) at the 38th (as of Oct 8, 2025), so positioning is light.
Re-grossing in banks into earnings leaves less capacity for fundamental investors to add to longs.
Possible squeeze post-CPI, with a derivative expression preferred over an RTY short.
Risks listed include a spike in bond vol or equity vol.
geopolitical: Houthis hit Aramco HQ and Iran has new Strait of Hormuz tactics (overnight escalatory headlines), pushing WTI up.
A US/Iran deal is named as the biggest catalyst and would squeeze EU and RTY higher.
Lagarde told France to fix its own debt, keeping European sovereign risk in view.
The Trump-Xi trade truce expires Nov 1, and NBC reports an agreed extension through Jan 20, 2027.
Upcoming political events: Brazil runoff Oct 25, Israel election Oct 27, US midterms Nov 3, APEC Nov 18-19, US funding deadline Dec 11, G20 Dec 15-16.

tension_points.bull_case: O'Dwyer says the selloff looks like quant/passive flow, the front end (3m5y) is unchanged, and 2s10s doesn't matter much, so fade the move and buy the group.
tension_points.bear_case: The curve is 5bps flatter on 2s10s, and re-grossing into the print leaves less capacity from fundamental investors to add to longs.

tension_points.bull_case: Hynix/Samsung updates point to ongoing thematic strength, ASML's beat-and-raise was rewarded, and SOX is well off its highs.
tension_points.bear_case: SOX fell five straight sessions, MU is lower pre-market, AI sentiment is fragile, and the OpenAI accounting story hurt confidence.
tension_points.what_invalidates: A tech earnings miss, such as a disappointing TSMC print and guide on Thursday, or a momentum/tech unwind.

tension_points.bull_case: A soft core print near 0.18% MoM keeps the market from pricing an October hike and lowers yields globally.
tension_points.bear_case: Headline CPI is expected at 0.55% MoM and growth continues to drive yields higher, with a Dec hike and 2 more in FY27 priced.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Core MoM well above the 0.18% forecast would reprice the October hike.
